approved: Carbon Credits and Other Legislation Amendment (Integrity and Transparency) Bill 2026
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would tighten rules and oversight for Australia's main carbon offset, greenhouse gas reporting and vehicle efficiency schemes.

It would replace an existing emissions committee with a new independent body, give native title claimants consent rights over carbon projects, and shift government carbon credit purchasing from the regulator to a department secretary.
The bill would let the minister stop carbon credits being issued under methods that face serious integrity risks, and change the purchasing principle from 'least cost' to 'value for money'.
Reforms the Australian Carbon Credit Unit Scheme's governance and consent processes.
Overhauls the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Scheme's integrity and transparency.
Fixes a timing issue in the New Vehicle Efficiency Standard's compliance rules.
Landholders including farmers and First Nations communities, businesses, vehicle suppliers, industrial facilities, and the Clean Energy Regulator.

Introducing the Carbon Credits and Other Legislation Amendment (Integrity and Transparency) Bill 2026, the Minister said it implements recommendations from the Chubb review and Climate Change Authority reviews, backed by more than $75 million committed since 2023, by requiring upfront native title consent for carbon farming projects and establishing a new independent Carbon Abatement Integrity Committee, which must include an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander member, to replace the existing methods assurance body. The bill also shifts responsibility for government carbon credit purchases to the department secretary under a new value-for-money test, introduces a Method Transition Declaration safeguard, and adjusts New Vehicle Efficiency Standard timelines.
